title: AskUserQuestion silently returns empty when called in the same turn as a Skill invocation
author: dicksontsai
body:
Thanks for the thorough investigation. This is the same root cause as #30363 — fixed in **v2.1.64**.

v2.1.63 (the version you're on) had a one-release regression in the permission pipeline: a new pre-classifier allow-rule check ran before the guard that keeps `AskUserQuestion` interactive. When *any* skill with `AskUserQuestion` in its `allowed-tools` is active in the turn (including marketplace plugin skills — several ship with it), the tool matched an auto-allow rule and skipped its own question UI.

The "same-turn vs next-turn" boundary you observed is the skill's `contextModifier` scope — it only modifies the tool-use context for the remainder of that turn.

Upgrading to v2.1.64+ resolves it.

title: [BUG] AskUserQuestion silently skipped when explicitly listed in skill's allowed-tools
author: dicksontsai
body:
Thanks for the clean minimal repro — this turned out to be a one-release regression.

**Fixed in v2.1.64.** The bug was introduced in v2.1.63 (one day earlier) by an internal change that added a pre-classifier allow-rule check in the permission pipeline. That check ran *before* the guard that keeps interactive tools like `AskUserQuestion` in the prompt flow — so listing `AskUserQuestion` in `allowed-tools` caused it to match an auto-allow rule and skip the question UI entirely (the question UI *is* the permission dialog for this tool).

Upgrading to v2.1.64 or later resolves it. You can keep `AskUserQuestion` in `allowed-tools` — it works correctly now.

Related: #30360 is the same root cause.

title: Bash permission heuristic misparses shell command boundaries (escaped semicolons treated as separators)
author: bcherny
body:
Thanks for the detailed report. This is fixed in **v2.1.89** (released 2026-03-31).

Root cause: in v2.1.85/86 the permission checker still used the legacy `shell-quote` parser, which treated `\;` as the operator `;` rather than a literal argument. After redirect/operator stripping the bare `2` from `2>/dev/null` survived as its own "subcommand", which is where the nonsensical "don't ask again for: 2" suggestion came from.

v2.1.89 replaced the shell-quote splitter with a real grammar parser. On current main, `find ... -exec ... \; 2>/dev/null | head -5` parses to exactly two subcommands (`find ...` and `head -5`) with `;` correctly inside argv — no spurious `2`.

The related "backslash before shell operator" false-positive warnings (#37391, #39655) were the same root cause and are also fixed in v2.1.89. Please upgrade and reopen if you still see it.
